{{c|{{x-larger|OF IESVS CHRIST ACCOR-}}}}
{{c|{{larger|DING TO LVKE.}}}}

{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text={{sc|The first}} part: of the Infancy both of the Precursor, and of CHRIST himself.}}{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. I.}}}}}}

{{c|''The Annunciation and Conception, first of the Precursor: 26. and sixe moneths after, of Christ also him self. 39. The Visitation of our Ladie, vvhere both the mothers doe prophecie. 57. The Natiuitie and Circuncision of the Precursor, where his father doth prophecie. 80. The Precursor is from a child an Eremite.''}} {{dropinitial|B|fl={{verse|chapter=1|verse=1}}}}ECAVSE many haue gone about to compile a narration of the things that haue been accomplished among vs: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=2}}† according as they haue deliuered vnto vs, vvho from the beginning them selues savv and vvere ministers of the vvord: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=3}}† it seemed good also vnto me {{sup|‖}} hauing diligently atteined to al things from the beginning, to vvrite to thee in order, good {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 1, 1.''}}* Theophilus, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=4}}† that thou maist knovv the veritie of those vvordes vvhereof thou hast been instructed.

{{verse|chapter=1|verse=5}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''1. Par. 24, 10.''}}* There vvas in the daies of Herod the king of Ievvrie, a certaine Priest named Zacharie, of the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the eue of S. Iohn Baptist.}}course of Abia: and his vvife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name Elizabeth. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=6}}† And they vvere both {{sup|‖}} iust before God, vvalking {{sup|‖}} in al the commaundements and {{sup|‖}} iustifications of our Lord vvithout blame, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=7}}† and they had no sonne: for that Elizabeth vvas barren, and both vvere vvel striken in their daies. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=8}}† And it came to passe: vvhen he executed the priestly function in the order of his course before God, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=9}}† according to the custome of the Priestly function, he vvent forth by lot {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 3, 17.''}}* to offer incense, entring into the temple of our Lord: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=10}}† and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lev. 16, 16.''}}* al the multitude of the people vvas {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ We see here that the Priest did his dutie within, the people in the meane time praying without: and that the Priests functions did profite then, though they neither heard nor saw his doings.}}∷ praying vvithout at the houre of the incense. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=11}}† And there appeared to him an Angel of our<noinclude>{{rh|||Lord,}}</noinclude>
